sections.html:
Land Services, a single department, assesses property and collects the tax in Crow Wing County. It is at 322 Laurel Street in Brainerd, the county seat, and answers at 218-824-1010.

The staff there mail bills, take payments, field valuation questions and maintain the field books and parcel records that anyone can research on the lower level. The county's Property Search website shows parcel data, and you can pull a duplicate tax statement by parcel ID or address.

Crow Wing is lake country in east central Minnesota, with roughly 417 named lakes, the Mississippi running through, and wooded rolling ground across 999 square miles of land. About 69,132 people live here, up 4.6% from the 2020 base.

The county counts 44,306 housing units and 29,402 households. In 2020 about 32.9% of units were vacant, which points to a big stock of cabins. Owners live in 77.0% of occupied homes, and the typical value is $306,800. Builders took out 625 permits in 2025. Brainerd, Baxter, Crosby, Crosslake, Garrison, Nisswa, Pequot Lakes, Breezy Point, Deerwood and Fort Ripley are among the communities.

With so much lakeshore, classification does a lot of work. A homestead and a seasonal cabin are taxed under different rules, so confirm which one your parcel carries before you price it.

A real estate bill is paid in halves, the first due May 15 and the second due October 15. Farmland has until November 15 for its second half. Mobile homes are billed on August 31 and November 15.

A resort or business that earns more than 60% of its gross income between May and August can file an affidavit moving the first-half date to May 31, and the affidavit has to go in with the payment. Any real estate half left unpaid is already carrying penalty.

Tax still open on December 31 of its due year turns delinquent. For delinquent years, the county wants a call to Land Services at 218-824-1010 before you pay, so the amount is right. Under Minnesota Statutes section 280.39, payments are applied to the newest years first.

A state-set table drives the penalty, and the county posts it. An unpaid first half climbs the fastest, as the county's figures show.

Penalty on an unpaid first half

May 162%4%

Manufactured homes pay 8% from September 1 on the first half, and personal property pays 8% from May 16. The treasurer may also abate a penalty once when a check was mailed with a postmark within a business day of the deadline.

Land Services takes payment four ways.

  • Online: an e-check costs $1.95, and a card costs 2.35% of the payment or $1.95, whichever is greater, up to $50,000. The processor keeps those fees, not the county. Credit takes three to four days to post.
  • For online payment you need the 8-digit parcel number, and you choose Pay Full Year to settle both halves.
  • At the counter, weekdays from eight to 4:30, with an outdoor drop box that is always open.
  • By mail: send the remittance stub and payment to Land Services, 322 Laurel Street Ste 15, Brainerd, MN 56401.

sections.h2: How values are set and how to push back
sections.html:
Every parcel is revalued each year, and the county must land between 90% and 105% of market value. Staff walk each property once every five years and check building permits. Comparable sales drive the number, adjusted for land, size, quality and condition, and the class follows current use.

Two routes exist for a disagreement. The first runs through the boards: a local board or open book meeting, then the county board, which you must phone ahead to be placed on. Where a city or township has no local board, owners go to an open book session before the county board. The second route is the Minnesota Tax Court.

  • Meeting times and places are printed on your Notice of Valuation and Classification.
  • You can appear in person, send a letter, or authorize a representative.
  • A court petition is due April 30 of the year the bill is payable (section 278.01).

The county's Taxes page points to Minnesota Department of Revenue guidance for owners who might pay less. Many need a filing before a deadline, so ask Land Services which fit your parcel.

  • Homestead classification and the homestead market value exclusion for owner-occupied houses.
  • Special homestead classification for blind or disabled owners.
  • Senior citizen property tax deferral.
  • A market value exclusion for owners with a service-connected disability.
  • 2c managed forest land and the Sustainable Forest Incentive Act.
  • Green Acres and rural preserve deferral for agricultural and rural vacant land, plus special agricultural homestead.
  • Property tax refunds.

An owner who is behind can pay part of a bill. The treasurer may take less than the full installment, and section 279.01 sends the money to the oldest unpaid installment first. A short payment goes to accrued penalty before tax. Partial payment does not satisfy the minimum needed to keep an appeal alive.

Delinquent tax stops recording: the auditor must clear the land first (section 272.12). A sale over $3,000 also brings a certificate of real estate value (section 272.115), and the seller's homestead class falls away until the buyer applies and qualifies.

Request a payoff for each parcel from Land Services, since lake property sales often include several. A buyer may also care about the relief programs the assessing office lists, such as 2c managed forest, the disability exclusion, Green Acres, homesteading and rural preserve.

For a clean closing, gather the parcel IDs, check the Property Search site for open balances, and bring the figures to your title company early so the payoff comes out of proceeds.

sections.h2: Before you list a Crow Wing property
sections.html:
Start at Land Services with three questions. What class does each parcel carry, homestead or seasonal? Is any half of this year's bill still open, or any older year? When was the property last walked by an appraiser? The answers shape your asking price and the payoff the title company will request.

If you rent the place out part of the year, the class may differ from what you assume. A lake cabin used by family only, with no one living there year-round, is not a homestead, and a buyer who plans to live there must file for the class on their own.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Crow Wing County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay Land Services at 322 Laurel Street Ste 15 in Brainerd, online, by mail or in the drop box. The counter is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 218-824-1010.

faqs.q: What are the Crow Wing County due dates?
faqs.a: Real estate is due May 15 and October 15, the agricultural second half on November 15, and mobile homes on August 31 and November 15. Each new year brings the same schedule.

faqs.q: How much is the late penalty on a Crow Wing County homestead?
faqs.a: It begins at 2% on an unpaid first half after May 15 and reaches 8% by October 1. Non-homestead property starts at 4% and tops out at 12%.

faqs.q: Can I challenge my Crow Wing County valuation?
faqs.a: Yes, through the local and county boards each spring and June, or by Tax Court petition due April 30 of the year the tax is payable. Call Land Services at 218-824-1010 and ask for the assessor.

faqs.q: Do delinquent Crow Wing County taxes need to be paid before a sale?
faqs.a: Yes, the deed cannot be recorded until they are cleared. Call Land Services at 218-824-1010 before paying so staff can confirm the right amount and avoid extra penalty.
